title: Stochastic quant divergence scratchpad
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent divergence / NaN regressions seen after switching to fp8 e4m3 kernel for 1.2B transformer variant.
- Failures are stochastic: only reproduced ~2/20 runs on the same instance. More common under longer context (>=1024).

Observed symptoms (examples):
- Downstream loss becomes NaN during evaluation. Sometimes logits are all -inf for a token step.
- Traces show layernorm and softmax producing inf/NaN.
- No OOM. CUDA memory stable.

Minimal repro (local):
- Model: small transformer 1.2B, checkpoint v2025-10-21, tokenized with our tiktoken fork.
- Quant config used: fp8 = {format: e4m3, per_tensor: true, stochastic_rounding: true, outlier_clip: 1e2}
- Env: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.3, cudnn 9.3, driver 535.xx, pytorch 2.2, custom runtime commit a1b2c3d

Commands tried:
1) baseline run (float32):
python eval.py --model ckpt/1.2b-fp32 --seq_len 512 --batch 8 --seed 42
-> stable, no NaNs after 200 eval steps

2) fp8 enabled (stochastic rounding ON):
python eval.py --model ckpt/1.2b-fp8 --quant-config configs/fp8-e4m3.json --seq_len 512 --batch 8 --seed 42
-> sometimes NaN after 60-120 steps

3) fp8 deterministic (stochastic rounding OFF):
python eval.py --model ckpt/1.2b-fp8 --quant-config configs/fp8-e4m3-deterministic.json --seq_len 512 --batch 8 --seed 42
-> failure rate drops but still happens ~1/20 runs

4) increase clip to 1e4 (disable clipping practically):
python eval.py --model ckpt/1.2b-fp8 --quant-config configs/fp8-e4m3-clip1e4.json --seq_len 512 --batch 8 --seed 42
-> no clear change in repro frequency

5) run with short seq_len 128:
python eval.py --seq_len 128 --seed 42
-> no NaNs observed across multiple runs (n=40)

6) run with longer seq_len 2048 (server):
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python eval.py --seq_len 2048 --batch 4 --seed 7 --quant-config configs/fp8-e4m3.json
-> higher failure rate (approx 30%)

Quick stack snippet when failure occurs:
  File \"runtime/inference.py\", line 438, in forward_step
    attn_out = softmax(attn_scores / sqrt_dk)
  File \"extensions/kernels/softmax_fp8.cu\", line 97, in softmax_fp8
    if (!isfinite(x)) { atomicAdd(&nan_counter, 1); }
RuntimeError: Assertion failed: isfinite detected NaN in softmax input

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Accumulation / rescaling error in KV-cache rescales when mixing fp8/int8 layers -> inf propagation. Happens with long context due to repeated rescale operations.
2) Stochastic rounding interaction with attention softmax leads to occasional huge positive logits (outliers) that blow up softmax denominator.
3) Per-tensor quantization is insufficient for heavy-tailed outlier weights in some attention heads; per-channel might mitigate.
4) Tiny denorm handling differences across kernels (our fp8 kernel vs reference) produce subnormal values that become zeros after certain ops, leading to division by zero in normalization.
5) Seed-dependent RNG for stochastic rounding not fully reseeded across worker threads -> correlated rounding causing drift.

Experiments performed / notes:
- Set stochastic_rounding=false -> reduced but not eliminated. Suggests stochastic rounding is a contributor but not the sole cause.
- Switched per_tensor->per_channel quantization for attention QKV weights: immediate reduction in NaN incidence in short runs (n=10).
- Instrumented KV-cache rescale counters: found occasional rescale factor > 1e6 at step ~512 on long sequences. Traced back to repeated feed-forward residual scaling where small numerical differences accumulated.
- Replaced our kernel softmax_fp8 with slower reference fp32 fallback for failed batches: runs to completion (suggests kernel underflow/overflow handling bug).

Quick patches tried (local):
- Add small epsilon to softmax denom: denom = max(sum(exp(x - m)), 1e-12) -> prevented crash in one run but masks root cause.
- Force denormals-are-zero (DAZ) off/on via env and recompile flags: minor effect.
- Disable KV-cache rescale optimization: dramatically reduces NaNs but increases latency by ~18%.

Logs / counters to add (next):
- Track per-head max(|logit|) distribution at every step and persist for failed runs.
- Record rescale factors and cumulative product for KV-cache at each step.
- Dump RNG state for stochastic rounding when NaN occurs (seed, thread ids).

Next experiments (planned):
1) Run long-seq runs with per-channel quant for QKV only and stochastic_rounding=false across n=100 runs.
2) Re-run with fp8 kernel compiled with fast-math off and check denorm behavior.
3) Add guard clipping before softmax (clip logits to +/- 50) and observe if NaNs drop (temporary mitigation).
4) Inject synthetic outlier weights into attention head and validate per-channel vs per-tensor behavior.
5) Reproduce on different GPU arch (A100 vs H100) to check if driver/arch-specific FP8 handling differs.

Slack threads / context: #eng-quant (see thread t/quant-nan-2026-03), linked PR attempts: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/987 (softmax fallback), jira INF-1324 (incident ticket).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Get ledger of which checkpoints were converted with per-tensor vs per-channel by conversion script (scripts/convert_to_fp8.py).
- Add deterministic logging wrapper to quant kernels to dump first nan-producing tensor to /tmp/quant-dumps/<runid>.npy.
- Coordinate with Noor (kernel owner) to add extra isfinite checks and a reproducible test harness in CI.

Bottom line: multiple signals point to a compound problem: kernel numerics + rescale accumulation + quantization granularity. Short term mitigations: per-channel for attention, disable KV rescale optimization on customer-critical flows, and add guard clipping. Need a proper kernel fix and CI repro harness.

Experimental results (raw):
- fp32 baseline: 0/500 runs failed
- fp8 e4m3 per-tensor stochastic: 18/100 failed (seq_len 2048)
- fp8 e4m3 per-channel stochastic: 4/100 failed
- fp8 e4m3 per-channel deterministic: 1/100 failed
- fp8 e4m3 per-channel deterministic + softmax-guard clip(50): 0/100 failed

Contact if you pick this up: Samira Ortiz (samira.ortiz@redwood.ai), office: Eng-HQ, ping on Slack @samira.

End of scratchpad.
